Subject: MAP — technical evaluation kickoff (recap & next steps)

Hi Sara / Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap of what we agreed and immediate next steps so we can get the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) moving: 

Key goals (from HealthGrid):
- Validate latency and per-token cost targets for user-facing summarization flow (500–800 token requests).
- Confirm model shortlist that meets accuracy and hallucination tolerances for clinical language.
- Verify data handling & KV cache behavior for patient PII (audit trail requirement).

Immediate MAP milestones we proposed:
1) Technical evaluation plan v1 (benchmark matrix + success criteria) — Redwood to deliver by Fri 11/27.
2) Tech kickoff with HealthGrid engineering — target 11/30 (2-hour deep dive).
3) Trial environment access & sample dataset (HealthGrid) — target 12/3.
4) Evaluation run & results review — target 12/10.

Owners we assigned on call:
- Redwood: Rafael Mendes (technical lead) + Marcus Lin (benchmarks & infra).
- HealthGrid: Alex Turner (platform) + Dr. Sara Patel (clinical accuracy owner).

Dependencies / blockers noted:
- HealthGrid to share a de-identified sample set and IP allowlist for trial infra.
- Procurement needs draft SOW + pricing ballpark for trial capacity.

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (draft milestones) and benchmark-matrix.xlsx (placeholder).

Action items for Sara / Alex: please confirm the sample data timeline and whether we should use your AWS account or Redwood sandbox for initial runs.

I'll loop Rafael & Marcus in on the follow-ups.

Thanks,
Grace
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: MAP — technical evaluation kickoff (recap & next steps)

Adding our internal ops plan and proposed benchmark slate: 

Grace — thanks for the summary. Rafael here — I'll lead the evaluation. Quick plan and acceptance criteria proposal for Rafael/Marcus to own and send as the benchmark-matrix.xlsx update by 11/27 end of day: 

Benchmark slate (initial shortlist):
- open-research-tuned-7B (quantized) — baseline cost-efficient candidate.
- clinical-llm-7B (community) — expected higher accuracy on clinical language, higher cost.
- redwood-compat-13B (FP16) — Redwood-verified performance profile, expected better latency for 500–800 token windows.

Success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation <450ms for 500-token prompts (Redwood sandbox, 1 concurrent user simulated).
- Cost: per-request token cost must be <= $0.004 (token calculations will be included in matrix).
- Accuracy: clinical hallucination rate <2% on critical fields per HealthGrid rubric.
- Stability: no KV-cache miss rate >1% during a 1-hour sustained load test (burst scenario).

Dependencies:
- HealthGrid sample dataset availability (per Sara: 12/1).
- Procure sign-off on sandbox usage and trial SOW (Grace to coordinate).
- We may need permission to enable prefix caching; Marcus will confirm whether that requires additional infra changes.

Marcus — can you validate the latency target on the redwood-compat-13B hypothesis (I think on T4-equivalent we can hit ~380ms p95 if caching is enabled). If so we'll mark redwood-compat-13B as our canary and run an A/B against the quantized 7B.

I'll attach an updated benchmark matrix and initial run plan.

Rafael
Staff ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: benchmark-matrix.xlsx
